findings.message: When a span has no hljs- class, such as a sub-language wrapper like `language-xml`, hljsRuns gives it the class of the span around it (`stack.push(cls!==undefined?cls:cur())`). The approved postcondition says such a span is read as classless text. The test in diff-highlight.test.ts pins the inheriting behaviour: 'inside a classed span it takes that span's class'. So text inside a wrapper nested in a string or comment is coloured with the outer class instead of being left classless. The doc comment in diff-highlight.ts also describes the inheriting behaviour, not the approved one.
findings.expectationRef: LLD contractDetails.api[renderRegistryWebviewSource].postconditions: 'a span whose class has no hljs- prefix (a sub-language wrapper) is read as classless text, not as a reason to reject'; PLAN t3 summary: 'a class with no hljs- prefix is classless'

findings.message: `type Run = { text: string; cls?: string }` declares an optional property without an explicit `| undefined`. The rule requires `cls?: string | undefined`, and the sibling chat-shell.test.ts follows it (`attach?: boolean | undefined`).
The `registry(opts: { withHljs?: boolean; hljs?: unknown })` parameter type declares `withHljs?` without `| undefined`. It should be `withHljs?: boolean | undefined`.
`interface Row { ...; added?: number; removed?: number }` declares optional properties without `| undefined`. They should be `added?: number | undefined; removed?: number | undefined`.

The generator script reports with `console.log` rather than a logger. This is a standalone build script outside the daemon's `shared/logger.js` tree, and it matches the existing `console.log` for the marked output in the same file, so this is idiom continuity rather than a clear breach.

findings.message: Graph grounding caveat. Every changed file came back with empty testsReaching. These are diff-level file entities with no symbol or test edges, not real coverage gaps. I ran the Story's 8 test files directly (`npx tsx --test --test-reporter=tap` on webview-hljs, diff-highlight, diff-tokens, diff-click, fake-dom, chat-theme, chat-shell and link-markup): 55/55 pass. That run includes all 20 automatable promised tests. The generator script itself has no test that runs it. Only its committed output (webview-hljs.ts) is checked: no script-tag text, under the 250 KB budget, and the language subset is registered. Its escaping and budget-throw branches are never exercised directly. Acceptable for a build-time generator.

diffTokens rebuilds the diff-line classification that fillDiff also does: a leading '\\' marks a note, '-' a removed line, '+' an added line, anything else context. fillDiff applies the same rules in its own loop a few lines below. If one copy changes and the other doesn't, the token runs will land on the wrong rows. A side-mismatch is caught by the line-count check and falls back to plain text, but a class mismatch would not be caught. A small shared lineKind(c) helper used by both would remove the second copy.

onDiffClick wraps its whole body in try{...}catch(x){} with an empty catch. Any failure while resolving the clicked line's path or line, or inside the LDEC sink, is dropped without a trace, so a broken click-to-open fails silently in the webview. diffTokens' catch is a deliberate fall-back to plain text. This one is not, so it should at least log, or narrow the try to the getSelection call.

diffTokens runs every time fillDiff runs: on first render, on each in-place redraw for a `replaces` row, and for every restored or paged-in diff row. Each run synchronously highlights the whole section twice, once for the old side and once for the new, even though only the first DIFF_LIMIT lines are shown until the widget opens. With many diff rows, such as a restored session or older pages, this all happens on the webview's main thread. The cost is bounded by the section size the host stores, so this is a performance note, not a correctness defect.
